The Personalisation Paradox

Different teams. Different priorities. One workspace that makes everyone work harder than necessary. Maya has the information she needs to manage customer accounts; the problem is finding the right signals across a workspace designed to serve everyone in the same way.

Illustrative scenario: Maya, Orbit and the account details are fictional. The problem framing and proposed experience are hypotheses to validate.

MAYA'S WORKDAY · 01/12

Meet Maya.

Maya leads Customer Success at a growing B2B SaaS company. She works across three teams and more than 120 customer accounts, from onboarding through renewal.

3 teamsCustomer Success · Support · Operations
120+ accountsFrom onboarding to renewal

Before the day gets busy, Maya needs to identify at-risk accounts, understand what changed, and see who owns the next follow-up.

MAYA'S WORKDAY · 02/12
MONDAY / 9:08 AM

The team check-in starts in ten minutes.

Maya wants to know which accounts are showing signs of risk, what changed overnight and which follow-ups are still open.

ORBIT / SHARED DEFAULT WORKSPACE
MAYA'S WORKDAY · 03/12
ORBIT / HOME

Customer Success, Sales and Finance all land on the same dashboard—even though each team starts the day with different decisions to make.

Usage charts, task lists, reports and activity all compete for space. Some matter to Maya; much of it has little to do with the decisions she needs to make this morning.

ORBIT / SHARED HOME
MAYA'S WORKDAY · 04/12
NORTHSTAR LABS / ACCOUNT

A renewal risk is hiding across several screens.

Northstar Labs' use of a key feature has fallen. Two support requests remain unresolved. The renewal is 18 days away.

No single view brings those details together. Maya has to move between pages before she can see the pattern.

NORTHSTAR LABS / CUSTOMER SIGNALS
MAYA'S WORKDAY · 05/12
MAYA'S MORNING

Maya has to visit several parts of Orbit before she can decide what needs action.

She checks usage, switches to support, finds the renewal date and compares account notes. Only then can she decide what needs action.

Orbit stores the information. Maya is left to connect it and work out what matters.

MAYA / MONDAY MORNING
MAYA'S WORKDAY · 06/12
ORBIT / HOME SETTINGS

Give each role a useful starting view—not a different product.

A Finance lead and a Customer Success lead may use the same platform, but they arrive with different questions and responsibilities.

Keep the same navigation, data model and permissions. Change the default dashboard modules and their order so each role sees its key measures, alerts and next actions first.

Personalisation should help people get oriented faster, without asking them to build a workspace from scratch.
ORBIT / ROLE-BASED HOME
MAYA'S WORKDAY · 07/12
MAYA'S WORKSPACE

Maya opens Orbit and sees the accounts that need attention.

The first view groups accounts with falling usage, unresolved support cases and renewals due soon. Each item shows the signal, its date, the account owner and a suggested next action.

The rest of Orbit is still one click away. Her starting view simply does more of the sorting.

ORBIT / MAYA'S WORKSPACE
MAYA'S WORKDAY · 08/12
NORTHSTAR / NEXT ACTION

This time, Maya can act without piecing the story together.

Maya sees Northstar's falling usage beside its open support issues and renewal date. She assigns an owner and schedules a customer check-in from the same workspace.

The usage drop, open support cases and renewal date now sit together. Maya can assign an owner and schedule the check-in without piecing the account story together herself.

NORTHSTAR LABS / ACTION PLAN
MAYA'S WORKDAY · 09/12
SUCCESS METRICS / HYPOTHESES

The first screen should help each role reach its most frequent decision with fewer page changes.

Test whether the role-based dashboard reduces time from sign-in to the first account action, increases completion of follow-ups, and improves weekly use of the account-risk workflow.

EXPERIMENT / HYPOTHESES TO TEST
MAYA'S WORKDAY · 10/12
WORKSPACE / USER CONTROL

Personalisation fails when setup takes more work than it saves.

If people must build a workspace from scratch, setup becomes another burden. If the defaults are too rigid, the original problem remains.

Give each role a preconfigured dashboard. Let users reorder or hide a limited set of modules. Keep navigation, permissions, records and shared workflows consistent so teams still work from the same product.

ROLE-RELEVANT DEFAULTS, WITH LIMITED FLEXIBILITY
MAYA'S WORKDAY · 11/12
THE PRODUCT PRINCIPLE

Personalise the starting point. Keep the product coherent.

One product can serve different roles without fragmenting the experience: keep the underlying workspace shared, and tailor the first screen to the decisions each role makes most often.

ONE PRODUCT, A MORE RELEVANT START
